members.claim: Search terms are normalized with TagList/Tag rules, not with StatisticsUtil.normalizeText(), which is what the note text goes through. Tag normalization (case, spaces turned into separators, stripped or kept punctuation such as apostrophes or hyphens) does not necessarily match the word tokenizer. So a valid search like "Isn't", "e-mail" or a term with surrounding punctuation can silently return 0 occurrences. A term with spaces (e.g. "hello world") can never match because note text is split on whitespace. Run each term through normalizeText() and split/trim it the same way findWords does.

findings.reason: normalizeText appends every `'` character and findWords splits only on whitespace, with no trimming of apostrophes from tokens. Quoted words therefore become separate entries in the unique count, the top list and search matching. It is a counting-accuracy issue, kept at low.
findings.claim: normalizeText keeps leading and trailing apostrophes, so 'hello' (in single quotes) is counted apart from hello, and a lone apostrophe becomes a word.
findings.evidence: normalizeText keeps every apostrophe, including leading/trailing ones used as single quotes. So 'hello' becomes the token "'hello'", which is counted separately from "hello". A standalone ' becomes its own 'word'. This inflates the new unique-word count, splits occurrence counts in the top-words list, and makes specific-word searches miss quoted occurrences. Consider trimming leading/trailing apostrophes from each token in findWords.
